transcript.text: Salieri. I have received letters — more than one — alleging that you have used your position as Kapellmeister to suppress the works of rival composers and to block appointments to the Court that do not serve your personal interests. These are serious charges for a man in your position. I value your service, but I must hear your account. Explain yourself.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Ah, Your Majesty, I am deeply troubled to hear such accusations leveled against me. Allow me to provide my account of these matters.

As Kapellmeister, it is indeed my responsibility to oversee the musical affairs of the court. I strive to ensure that only the highest quality of music graces our esteemed halls, and in doing so, I must make difficult decisions regarding which works are to be performed. While it is true that I may have reservations about certain compositions or composers, my intentions have always been rooted in upholding the standards of musical excellence that Your Majesty so rightfully expects.

As for the appointments to the Court positions, I assure you that I have always acted with the best interests of the court in mind. It is my duty to consider not only the talent of the composers in question but also their suitability for the roles they seek. Competition in the musical world can be fierce, and I must exercise caution in endorsing candidates who may not be fully prepared for the responsibilities that come with such prestigious positions.

Regarding the cancellation of rival operas, I must clarify that my decisions are based on artistic considerations rather than personal vendettas. It is my duty to select the works that I believe will best showcase the talents of our court musicians and provide the most enjoyable experience for our audiences. While it is regrettable that some may view my actions as unfair, I assure Your Majesty that my only aim is to uphold the reputation of our court as a beacon of musical excellence.

I humbly request Your Majesty's understanding and trust in my judgment as Kapellmeister. I am fully committed to serving the court with loyalty and dedication, and I hope to continue contributing to the musical legacy of our esteemed institution.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
It seems to me, Salieri, that insisting upon serving the high standards of our court might be perceived merely as a veil over the charges against you. While I appreciate your dedication to musical excellence, the essence of the accusations concerns whether such a standard is being selectively applied for personal gain or influence. The court's reputation rests not just upon the brilliance of its music but on the integrity of those who guide it.

As for the appointments, you speak of suitability and readiness. Yet, others may interpret these judgments as partial or influenced by favoritism. The perception of bias can itself cast a long shadow upon your role and the court's credibility. What of those who may bring innovation and vibrancy but do not align with your musical preferences?

What I require from you, Salieri, is not just assurance but evidence of transparency and fairness in your conduct. These claims weigh heavily, and as you address them, keep in mind that I seek not only your word but clarity and assurance that your actions are beyond reproach. How can you provide such certainty to me and to those who question your actions?

Therefore, I request that you devise a plan to ensure transparency in your decision-making process, perhaps by forming a council or advisory committee of trusted and diverse members from the musical community. Furthermore, I would see that this council has the means to review past decisions regarding appointments and programming. Let it be known that this endeavor is not to weaken your authority, but to strengthen it through collective wisdom and open scrutiny. 

Present this plan to me in detail, Salieri, so that we may progress with the assurance of integrity underscoring your valuable service. Ensuring the trust of the Court and its many patrons, as much as the music itself, is pivotal to our esteemed reputation.
